analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift, a test-only file. The visible lines (1756-3038) are unchanged context. The only changed range is head 3140-3240, which falls outside the supplied units. It adds tests that a whole-root maintainer remembers header-ownership verdicts only for unchanged files, keyed on ctime and size, and that a replaced lookalike is re-read. I could not verify those tests or the production SSDWholeRootMaintainer change. A test-only change does not alter runtime security behavior.

The visible tests exercise controls from T-041. They cover the ready-receipt no-emit matrix: too-short, rate-limited, eviction, shutdown and corrupt-file cases. They cover staging reservation release on success, cancel, close, backstop and deadline refusal. They cover shared-entry reservation charged once, with per-request tickets that an unrelated request ID cannot consume. They cover instance-namespaced reservations. They cover the pre-write free-space reserve including the pending donation, and a write-outcome classification matrix. They cover the kv3 root being isolated from the legacy kv root. They cover whole-root TTL and global disk-budget enforcement on unloaded model directories, and epoch preservation across eviction.

These assert the intended invariants: fail closed on corruption, balanced reservation release, and no epoch rotation from eviction. They do not weaken any assertion that I can see. Test fixtures use in-memory or temp-dir keys only, with no secrets.

Open question for integration: the maintainer's verdict-cache production code (outside these units) should be reviewed. The point is that a cached ownership verdict keyed on ctime/size cannot be abused to make the maintainer delete or spare files outside the dedicated root. That code is not in the supplied evidence, so I record it as an unverified contract rather than a finding.
